content.text: This confirms a genuine CARD-0159 regression, unrelated to CARD-0231: `ClassifyReportAsync`'s new one-nudge-then-continue contract (`server/Application/Services/AgentTaskReplyService.cs:1809`) means any caller/self-owned task whose reply doesn't carry an explicit `[antiphon-report:...]` closing line…

input.command:
mkdir -p "C:/Users/lndco/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--src-Antiphon/cefed08a-fd4a-42a0-8c76-0fbf82cf6b20/scratchpad"
cat > "C:/Users/lndco/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--src-Antiphon/cefed08a-fd4a-42a0-8c76-0fbf82cf6b20/scratchpad/card-regression-desc.md" <<'EOF'
CARD-0159 (`eab67a3`, merged tonight) changed `ClassifyReportAsync`
(`server/Application/Services/AgentTaskReplyService.cs:1786`) so that a task's turn ending
without an explicit `[antiphon-report:<id> done|blocked|failed]` closing line no longer settles
in that turn — it withholds settlement, sends a one-time WhenIdle nudge asking for the closing
line, and returns `null` (task stays Dispatched/Working). Settlement now only happens either
immediately (with a verdict marker), or on the SECOND unmarked turn end (after the nudge), or
never if the session isn't live to receive the nudge.

This silently broke a pre-existing test that has been green since CARD-0047
(`d187c62`, months old, untouched since): `AgentTaskCheckSweepTests.
the_same_caller_turn_DOES_settle_when_the_prompt_carries_its_own_marker`
(tests/Antiphon.Tests/Application/AgentTaskCheckSweepTests.cs:461). It seeds a caller/self-owned
task (Role=Plan, Kind=Orchestrator, `AgentSessionId == callerSessionId` — "the orchestrator's own
chunk"), sends one turn whose PROMPT carries the task's own marker and whose REPLY is a plain
completion sentence with no closing verdict line ("Chunk owned: three delegates ran, all
merged."), and asserts the task settles to `Succeeded` in that same turn. It now asserts
`Dispatched`.

**Confirmed independent of any other card tonight**: reproduced on a completely clean checkout of
master at `87f11e0` (CARD-0159 + its CARD-0230 DI followup, nothing else) —
`dotnet run --project tests/Antiphon.Tests -- --treenode-filter "/*/*/AgentTaskCheckSweepTests/*"`
gives 1 failed / 30 succeeded, same test, same assertion (`parent.Status should be Succeeded but
was Dispatched`). It surfaced tonight only incidentally, while reviewing an unrelated card
(CARD-0231) whose branch got rebased onto CARD-0159's merge — `AgentTaskCheckSweepTests` was not
in CARD-0159's own verification list (8 other suites, 210 assertions) nor in the reviewer's
independent re-run list, so nothing caught it before it reached master.

**Open question for whoever picks this up** (a design call, not something to guess at 2am): is
the test's assertion now simply STALE — i.e. CARD-0159 intentionally requires a verdict marker or
a second (nudged) turn for every settlement path, and this test needs updating to model that new
two-step contract — or is the one-nudge-then-continue behavior an unintended regression for
caller/self-owned tasks specifically (an orchestrator's own "own the chunk" self-dispatch was
never taught to emit a closing `[antiphon-report:...]` line, and until every such prompt template
is updated, EVERY plain-language completion of a self-owned chunk will now cost an extra idle-turn
round trip before settling, or never settle if the session isn't live for the nudge). Whichever
way this resolves, `AgentTaskCheckSweepTests` needs to go green again, and CARD-0159's own S2
design intent should be read first (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-30-card-0159-settlement-positive-evidence-plan.md`).
EOF
